cultural.vision_reason: A strip-woven cotton textile with dark indigo ground, white check bands, and colorful supplementary-weft diamond patterning in the central panel — this narrow-strip weaving technique with polychrome geometric motifs is consistent with West African (Guinea-Bissau region) Papel textile production.

physical.title: textile
physical.summary:
Textile consisting of six narrow strip woven cotton lengths, hand sewn together selvedge to selvedge. Ground weave: plain weave: dyed blue warps and dyed blue and white wefts. This creates a cloth with a dark blue background with bands of weft stripes at either end in white. The cloth is then decorated using supplementary weft and supplementary weft floats. There are white check bands at each end of the textile which are flanked by the white stripes mentioned earlier. The central panel consists of weft stripes of a diamond based pattern in dyed red, yellow, green, blue and white cotton: the colour is consistant across the entire wedt of the fabric. There are also weft check bands at regular intervals in tinsel.

The textile is finished in unwork warps.
